context: Three-panel tidal harmonic decomposition: a 14-day composite time series (main), a cycle plot overlaying 14 daily traces, and a ridgeline KDE of amplitude distributions for 4 harmonic constituents (M2, S2, K1, O1) with toggle interactivity.
first_impression: Clean and well-composed — the dark theme, restrained 5-color palette, and clear visual hierarchy make a scientifically dense subject immediately readable.
what_works: The composite line is visually dominant (white, stroke-width 2) over the four faint harmonic traces (opacity 0.6), so the viewer always knows what to focus on; the three panels form a coherent conceptual unit rather than independent competing views. Spring/Neap tide annotations add domain context without clutter.
what_doesnt: The cycle plot's 14 overlapping day traces at 20% opacity are conceptually unfamiliar — a viewer without prior exposure to cycle plots may not understand what the faint lines represent versus the bold mean line. The main chart's 5 overlapping sinusoids become slightly tangled in the higher-frequency beat regions (Mar 22–24), though toggling helps.
